verdicts.factCheck: Fetched crates/mega-evm/src/block/limit.rs, block/executor.rs, block/chain.rs and constants.rs from mega-evm main and v1.7.4 on 2026-11-25; cmp reports all four pairs byte identical. limit.rs lines 880-890 on main return Err for every candidate once block_state_growth_used is at or above block_state_growth_limit. Lines 387-399 select rex::BLOCK_STATE_GROWTH_LIMIT for Rex through Rex6, and constants.rs lines 206 and 211 set TX_STATE_GROWTH_LIMIT and BLOCK_STATE_GROWTH_LIMIT to 1000, so one transaction can exhaust the block budget. executor.rs commit_tx_result (about lines 580-600) says a rejected transaction returns Err before touching executor state and the caller decides what to do, typically putting it back in the pool. chain.rs lines 35-46 end the mainnet schedule at Rex6 (timestamp 1787626800). On https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc, eth_getBlockByNumber latest returned block 32,787,103 with baseFeePerGas 0xf4240 (1,000,000 wei), gasLimit 10,000,000,000 and timestamp 1795584114, which is after Rex6; web3_clientVersion returned mega-reth/v2.2.3-72527bc@mnet-ash-rpc-2. The 22.6 million gas cost for 1,000 new slots was not recomputed this cycle; it rests on the cycle 13 reading of constants.rs. No public source gives the sequencer's requeue order, so the amplified form remains unconfirmed.
verdicts.codeCheck: src/PoolManager.sol:103-113 (unlock with the NonzeroDeltaCount check at line 111), modifyLiquidity from line 145 and take at lines 291-297 have no dependence on block number, time or position in a block. A delayed call later runs with the same checks and the same toInt128 cast at line 294. _settle at lines 349-365 credits msg.value or the balance difference only, so a delay cannot move any delta or balance. The effect is liveness only and applies to every contract on the chain.
verdicts.corrections: The base effect (one filler closes the rest of its block to later candidates) is confirmed by source. Only the amplified form, in which N fillers close N consecutive blocks, depends on the unconfirmed queue rule of the closed sequencer, which is why the verdict is plausible. The coreRefs mark where victim calls enter and do not compute anything differently.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Monad main, the new per-block cache of literal memory ends in the x86 emitter (touched_memory_end_): can a compiled MLOAD or MSTORE skip a needed memory expansion?
clearedSpotChecks.note: Read emitter.cpp on main. begin_new_block (lines 1047-1062) resets touched_memory_end_ to 0 unless keep_stack_in_next_block_ is set. That flag is set only by jumpi_keep_fallthrough_stack (line 3907), which jumpi (lines 3533-3552) chooses only when the fall-through block is not in jump_dests_, so the release build keeps the cache only for a block with a single entry, not just in debug builds. At lines 6362-6372 the cache is updated before the emitted compare and expansion call; if expansion fails the frame exits, so no later access in that block runs. Literal offsets are bounded to Memory::offset_bits = 28 (runtime/types.hpp line 126, static_assert at emitter.cpp line 6328), so the int32 sum lit + read_size cannot overflow. Memory never shrinks within a frame and the data pointer is reloaded from the context on every cached access.
